intro: The small formulas that keep people on good terms: apologising, thanking, congratulating and sending regards.
p.gracias por.nota: Followed by a noun or an infinitive.
p.a ti.nota: The answer to gracias when you are grateful too.
p.que tengas suerte: good luck; hope you have good luck
p.encantado de conocerte: pleased to meet you (encantada for a female speaker)
p.mucho gusto: nice to meet you; pleased to meet you
b1.texto:
**Apologising.** You can add a reason with **es que**:

- **Lo siento, de verdad. Es que** había mucho tráfico.
- **Perdóname.** / **Perdóneme.** (usted)
- **Disculpa.** / **Disculpe.**
- **Ha sido sin querer.**

Common replies include **No importa**, **No pasa nada**, **No te preocupes** and **No tiene importancia**.

**Thanking.** **Gracias por todo**, **gracias por** la invitación, **gracias por** venir. After **por**, use a noun or infinitive. Common replies: **De nada** and **No hay de qué**. Say **A ti** when you are thanking the other person too.

**Promising.** **Te prometo que** no volverá a pasar. **Te lo prometo.**

**Congratulating.** **¡Enhorabuena!**, **¡Bien hecho!**, **¡Buen trabajo!** On a birthday: **¡Felicidades! Que cumplas muchos más.**

**Good wishes** use **que** + subjunctive: **que te diviertas**, **que descanses**, **que tengas suerte**, **que te vaya bien**, **que te mejores**. Replies include **Igualmente** and **Gracias, tú también**.

**Regards.** **Recuerdos a** tu familia; **saludos a** Pedro. Reply: **De tu parte.**

**Welcoming.** **Pasa, pasa, estás en tu casa. ¡Qué bien que estés aquí!**

**Introducing.** Informally: **Mira, este es Luis. Encantado/a de conocerte.** The speaker says **encantado** or **encantada** according to their gender. Formally: **Quisiera presentarle a la señora Ruiz. Mucho gusto.**
b2.titulo: Arriving late to a birthday dinner
b2.f0: At last! Come in, come in, make yourself at home.
b2.f1: Forgive me, really. The thing is, I missed the bus.
b2.f2: Never mind, it's not important. Look, this is my cousin Andrés.
b2.f3: Pleased to meet you. And you, Berta, happy birthday! Many happy returns.
b2.f4: Thank you for coming and thank you for the present.
b2.f5: Thank you for inviting me. By the way, my mother sends her regards.
b4.pregunta: Complete: thank you for helping me.
b5.pregunta: Someone says Dale recuerdos a tu padre. You answer…
b5.o0.refuerzo: I'll pass them on from you.
b6.pregunta: Someone steps on your foot and says ¡Perdón! You answer…
b7.pregunta: Complete the wish: have a good rest.
b7.o0.refuerzo: A wish with que takes the subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: A wish with que takes the subjunctive.
b8.o2.explicacion: The phrase means it was not on purpose.
b9.pregunta: Someone says ¡Que tengas un buen fin de semana! A natural answer is…
b10.traduccion: I promise it won't happen again.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write three short notes: an apology, a thank-you and congratulations.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Play both parts aloud: arrive late and apologise, be introduced, congratulate someone and send regards.
